stories.title: Former KP ministers Jhagra, Bangash among 3 PTI leaders held under MPO despite bail from PHC
summary: PESHAWAR: Former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa ministers Taimoor Saleem Jhagra and Kamran Bangash were among three PTI leaders taken into “preventative” custody by police shortly after they were granted interim bail by the high court.
Finally, at around 6pm, the PTI leaders left the barroom and were taken into custody by the police at the high court’s entrance.
Subsequently, the PTI leaders approached the ATC on Oct 29 seeking concession of interim pre-arrest bail, which was initially granted to them, the lawyers recalled.

stories.title: Over 170 major websites hit by attack, including BBC, Ikea and Air France: report
summary: Nearly 200 major websites, including those of the BBC, HSBC UAE bank, Air France and Ikea were targeted by a malicious cyber attack seeking to steal financial information and infect Apple devices, specialist media reported on Tuesday.

Optimizely confirmed the incident and said it had identified “a security incident in which an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects”.
The malicious script also sought to capture payment card details as users entered them, steal cookies and screenshots, and deploy exploit code targeting Apple’s iOS devices, Helme said.

stories.title: Tarar says referendum 'legal and constitutional' method of gauging public opinion on new provinces
summary: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that a referendum was a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces, adding that no political party should have reservations regarding it.

The minister said that there was an ongoing debate in the country regarding “good governance”. “The public wants a good government that is accountable … You and all of us have been part of this system for decades.

The minister added that the people could not be stopped from talking about something that was for their benefit. “Democratic and political processes demand that this debate be done by the people … What is the problem with going to the public?

stories.title: 8 Pakistan Bar Council members call on judiciary to take note of Imran's plea for medical treatment
summary: ISLAMABAD: Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Tuesday called upon the judiciary to ensure implementation of the Supreme Court’s (SC) order directing incarcerated ex-premier Imran Khan’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment.

The PBC members urged the government and its agencies to implement court orders and ensure that both Imran and his wife received proper medical treatment in accordance with the law and the Constitution.

The statement further highlighted that Imran had been kept in solitary confinement and denied due medical treatment and access to his legal team and family members, jeopardising his and his wife’s health.

stories.title: US proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards
summary: WASHINGTON: The United States Department of Labour has published sweeping proposed changes to the rules governing employment-based green cards, requiring companies to make greater efforts to recruit American workers before sponsoring foreign employees for permanent residency.

The proposed overhaul would extend recruitment periods, restrict sponsorship by companies that have recently laid off US workers and eliminate special exemptions currently available to certain healthcare professionals.

Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling said existing rules had allowed companies to sponsor foreign workers “without fully considering American applicants”, a practice the department seeks to address through “expanded recruitment and enforcement requirements”.

stories.title: Pakistan fall to India in SAFF final after late heartbreak
summary: Pakistan, appearing in their first-ever SAFF Championship final, began confidently and enjoyed the better of the opening exchanges, putting India’s reshuffled side under sustained pressure.

India, meanwhile, struggled to establish attacking rhythm, although they came close to scoring around the 35th minute when Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf Butt produced an important save to deny a dangerous effort.
Pakistan threw players forward during the closing stages in a desperate attempt to force an equaliser, but India held firm through five minutes of added time to secure victory.

stories.title: Jensen Huang says willing to return as Nvidia CEO, 'owns mistakes'
summary: The turmoil has battered shares in Nvidia, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company.
Tech tycoon Elon Musk and other major AI investors have been calling for Huang’s reinstatement with an open letter that has garnered more than 190,000 signatures.

He sounded a note of contrition. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” he said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret.

stories.title: Rs24bn additional QTA proposed by Discos draws protest from industrial consumers
summary: Javed, from Karachi, noted the Discos claimed Rs29.25bn of negative impact of the ICP on industrial consumers, saying it was actually an additional burden from all consumers.

Cumulatively, all 11 Discos reported that capacity charges during the July-September period had increased by Rs39bn, which also included the impact of system losses on the monthly fuel cost and variable operation and maintenance costs.
Seven out of the 11 Discos demanded additional recovery of about Rs37bn on account of capacity charges, variable O&M charges and the impact of T&D losses on monthly FCA.

stories.title: In hard-hitting speech, Bilawal says system was ‘made to collapse’
summary: The PPP chairman’s remarks went beyond his oft-repeated calls for electoral reforms and political consensus, as he called for the opposition PTI to be given reserved seats as a “confidence-building measure”.

Replying to a question about new provinces and a “reset”, Bilawal said the PML-N-led government had not discussed the matter with the PPP, adding that this raised the question of why this was “being made to discuss by the media”.

Bilawal remarked that the opposition had the “most patriotic” role in the Parliament. “For any government to question the patriotism of an opposition member [..] it is not only an injustice to that parliament or to the system, but the biggest injustice to the country,” he added.

stories.title: Pakistan’s pace trio routs Sri Lanka for 98 before hosts take control
summary: Pakistan’s fast bowlers dismissed Sri Lanka for a paltry 98 before the home side reached 121-3 on the opening day of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday, taking a 23-run lead into the close of play.
Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah and Aamer Jamal claimed three wickets apiece as Sri Lanka were bowled out in 35.3 overs after Pakistan won the toss and elected to field on a green-tinged pitch.
Awais, however, remained at the crease to guide Pakistan beyond Sri Lanka’s total.

stories.title: UK magazine listing points to loss of four Indian Rafales
summary: A British aviation magazine has listed 32 Rafale fighter jets as being in active service with the Indian Air Force (IAF), four fewer than the 36 aircraft New Delhi has officially said it operates, according to its latest World Air Forces directory for 2027.

Read: Trump says seven jets shot down in Pakistan-India conflict India signed a deal in 2016 to purchase 36 Rafale fighter jets from France for around $8.7 billion, marking its first major acquisition of combat aircraft in two decades.
In August 2025, Trump said seven aircraft had been shot down during the Pakistan-India conflict in May.

stories.title: 'Under the bus': Feuds grip Trump's White House after midterms
summary: From feuding officials stuck together on Air Force One to uncomfortable press conferences, rifts in President Donald Trump’s White House have spilt into the open after the US midterm elections.
Disagreements over China, AI and Iran have flared up, while personal rivalries in the West Wing that were bottled up for the first half of Trump’s second term have started to boil over.
Miller, the new chief of staff, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have struck up an “unlikely alliance” after being foes during Trump’s first term, the Wall Street Journal reported.

stories.title: PTA finalises licensing framework for 'sky-high' internet, telecommunication services
summary: It added that transit aircraft passing through Pakistani airspace would require a no-objection certificate from the authority, subject to applicable compliance requirements.

It said that the introduction of in-flight telecommunication services would “enhance passenger experience through seamless in-flight internet connectivity, enabling access to digital services, entertainment, personal communication and work-related activities”.

It added that the initiative would further strengthen the authority’s efforts to expand digital connectivity in Pakistan by “extending telecommunication services beyond terrestrial networks and enabling seamless connectivity during air travel”.

stories.title: Local govt polls in Punjab to be held in two phases
summary: In a letter to the Punjab chief secretary, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) said it had accepted the proposal conveyed by the province’s Local Government and Community Development Department secretary, in his letter dated Nov 16.
The ECP also forwarded copies of the letter to the provincial election commissioner and the secretary of the Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department.
The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013.

stories.title: Vehicles without fitness, emission tests to be barred from Islamabad to curb smog
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday decided to bar vehicles without fitness and emission testing from entering Islamabad, as part of measures to curb smog and air pollution in the capital.
The meeting reviewed the current smog situation in Islamabad, the Air Quality Index (AQI) and ongoing measures to control air pollution.
Chaudhry directed all relevant departments to ensure coordinated and effective measures to control air pollution and prevent smog.

stories.title: No casualties reported as huge blaze engulfs industrial unit in Karachi's Baldia Town
summary: KARACHI: A massive fire broke out at an industrial unit in Karachi’s Baldia Town on Tuesday morning, reportedly during the refilling of an underground oil tank by a tanker, rescue officials said.
Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaanul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that the fire had broken out in a factory that manufactured glass products.
The rescue official said that the fire had spread from the ground floor to the first and second floors. “All the floors were destroyed along with the raw material that was being stored there.

stories.title: Punjab replaces newly appointed Rawalpindi CPO within hours
summary: The Punjab government on Tuesday reversed its appointment of a new Rawalpindi city police officer (CPO) within hours of issuing the initial transfer orders, naming Sardar Ghiyas Gul to the post instead of Muhammad Sohail Ashraf in a swift reshuffle of senior police officers.
Following approval of his transfer, the provincial government issued a notification appointing grade-19 officer Ashraf as the new Rawalpindi CPO.

Read: CPO, SSP issued notices in Hina Javed case Gul has previously served in Rawalpindi as Saddar superintendent of police and chief traffic officer, besides holding the post of Attock district police officer.

stories.title: UK sanctions Israeli firms helping build West Bank settlements
summary: The Foreign Office, citing the UN, said “over 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins that humanitarian partners and donors purchased are outside Gaza ready to go in but are being held by the Israeli authorities”.
And it accused Israeli authorities of blocking “timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza”.

The UK’s Foreign Office also sanctioned Israeli activist group Tzav 9 on Tuesday for blocking aid deliveries into Gaza. “We will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza,” Miliband said.

stories.title: Pakistan discusses avenues for enhancing bilateral defence cooperation with UK, Turkiye
summary: According to the statement, the visit reflected the shared resolve of Pakistan and the UK to deepen defence cooperation and strengthen bilateral military ties.

Separately, Commander of the Turkish Air Force General Rafet Dalkıran also called on the CDF at GHQ, where matters of mutual interest, regional security dynamics and avenues to enhance bilateral defence cooperation were discussed, the military said.

The visiting dignitary reciprocated the strengthening of bilateral defence ties, appreciated the professionalism of the Pakistan Armed Forces and acknowledged the country’s contributions to regional peace and stability, the ISPR added.

stories.title: Top UN court ruling on Myanmar genocide to be watched for clues on Gaza
summary: The decision by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), also known as the World Court, will be its first substantive ruling in more than a decade on alleged violations of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Genocidal intent Legal scholars will be scrutinising the ruling for guidance that could resonate beyond ​Myanmar, including in South Africa's 2023 case accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza, an allegation Israel rejects.

Gambia brought the Rohingya case in 2019, arguing that Myanmar bears state responsibility ‌for genocide ⁠after a military offensive drove at least 730,000 Muslim Rohingya from Buddhist-majority Myanmar into neighbouring Bangladesh.

stories.title: Grand Theft Auto VI heads to launch amid feverish anticipation
summary: GTA V, released in 2013 by Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games and set in an alternative Los Angeles ​called Los Santos, was one of the best-selling video games of all time.

Singaporean gamer Julian Tay said in a social media post that he had drawn up a five-point "GTA VI Gaming Agreement" for his spouse, covering the first 10 days after launch and stipulating ​when missions could be interrupted and when hugs, kisses and errands were allowed.
That makes the launch a major ​test not just for Rockstar Games and owner Take-Two Interactive Software, but for a gaming market hit by slowing sales and weaker demand for ​aging consoles.

stories.title: New York Mayor Mamdani disbands 'notorious' police unit that used excessive force on protesters
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is disbanding a police unit criticised for using excessive force against ‌protesters in favour of a new "civilian-led approach" to large public demonstrations, he announced on Monday.

In the joint announcement alongside New York City Police ​Commissioner Jessica Tisch, Mamdani said he is creating a new civilian-led group called the Community Dialogue ⁠and De-escalation Division, whose members would be unarmed and would not have arrest powers.
At the New York Police Department, he said ​the disbanded SRG unit would be replaced in part by a new unit called the Patrol Support Division, which he said would ​police protests differently.

stories.title: Pakistan, Sri Lanka docked WTC points for slow over-rates in first Test
summary: Pakistan and Sri Lanka have been penalised for maintaining slow over-rates in the drawn first Test of their two-match ICC World Test Championship (WTC) series, with Pakistan losing five points and Sri Lanka suffering a 15-point deduction.

Match referee Dean Cosker of the ICC International Panel imposed the sanctions after Pakistan were found five overs short of the required rate and Sri Lanka 15 overs behind, after time allowances were taken into account.
Consequently, Pakistan were fined 25 per cent of their match fees, while Sri Lanka received the maximum 50 per cent fine.

stories.title: Trump meets key US regional allies in Manila ahead of China visit
summary: US President Donald Trump met the leaders of key regional allies India, Japan and ​Australia in the Philippines on Tuesday, at the start of an Asian trip that also includes a much-anticipated trilateral meeting, with his Chinese and Russian counterparts.

Trump arrived in the Philippine capital at ‌the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit, and began his three-day regional visit with the first meeting in two years of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific democracies.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, who will host Trump and others at a meeting ​this week of the 21-member Pacific Rim grouping APEC, has previously objected to the Quad as an effort to encircle Beijing.

stories.title: Autopsy reveals multiple injuries on teenage domestic worker found dead at FIA official’s residence in Islamabad
summary: ISLAMABAD: The autopsy report of a 13-year-old domestic worker, who was found dead at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) official on Sunday night, suggests that she had been subjected to repeated physical assaults.

Old burn scars on the back, a thickened scar on the right upper thigh, darkened and swollen skin around both knees and the left thigh, swelling in the knee joint and a non-healing wound on the outer side of the left knee were also found.
An Islamabad police officer said Fatima had been working as a domestic help at the official’s residence for a couple of years, dating back to when he was serving in the capital police.

stories.title: Nvidia's Huang signals willingness to return as CEO, board creates national security panel
summary: I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an… — Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang) November 17, 2026 Earlier in the day, Nvidia created a board-level committee to oversee national security and export controls, its first major ⁠governance move since Huang left.
The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora ​Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chair, Nvidia said.
The NVIDIA Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

stories.title: Petrol dips by Rs3, diesel remains unchanged for Nov 18
summary: The federal government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 while keeping the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) unchanged for November 18.
The revision comes a day after the government slashed the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2 per litre for November 17.

Read: Govt cuts petrol, high-speed diesel price by Rs2 On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Bilawal's statement on constitutional amendment could lead to 'disqualification', says Sanaullah
summary: Sanaullah said Bilawal's statement on Tuesday was driven by anger over the issue of Sindh's division, acknowledging that the PPP had reservations about any proposal to divide the province or create new provinces within it.
Sanaullah rejected the interpretation, insisting that Bilawal had made a political statement out of anger rather than admitting to any wrongdoing.

He also pointed out that the PPP was represented on the judicial commission formed to deliberate on the 27th Amendment, with Bilawal himself serving as one of the government's representatives alongside Sanaullah.

stories.title: Highly classified US national security communications network is down, CNN reports
summary: The highly classified network that ‌the US National Security Agency uses for its internal communications is down, CNN ​reported on Tuesday, citing five ​people familiar with the matter.
The NSA did not immediately return a message ​seeking comment about the reported outage.
US President ​Donald Trump on Tuesday played down ​the ⁠disruptions, saying such problems were inevitable.

stories.title: 'Death is near': Inside the hoax bomb threats that rattled Europe's schools and airports
summary: The October 19 threats also hit schools in Scotland, where Mimecast said at least 33 schools were targeted.

The ones sent to schools in Northern Ireland, Scotland and the Bulgarian ​institutions on October 19 carried the subject line “Death is near.” The messages were sent from at least four email accounts that Proofpoint and Mimecast said had been hijacked.
More ​than 50 flights at some 15 airlines received hoax bomb threats between November 2 and 6, according to flight tracking specialists AirNav Radar.

stories.title: India clinch record tenth SAFF Cup title
summary: Pakistan gradually took control, winning the first corner of the match in the sixth minute, which India's defence dealt with comfortably.
India finally threatened in the latter stages of the half when Suriavanshi connected with a volley on target, but Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf Butt produced an outstanding save.
Pakistan won another corner shortly before the break, but India's defence again held firm.

stories.title: Post-mortem documents 20 major wounds, visible marks of violence in death of 13-year-old domestic worker in Islamabad
summary: A senior Islamabad police officer told The Express Tribune that both suspects had been granted four-day physical remand by a district court.
He said the police had faced considerable pressure but registered the case and arrested the suspects, despite the girl’s father initially being reluctant to lodge a complaint.
Fatima died on November 14 at the residence of Ashraf, a senior Police Service of Pakistan officer posted at the FIA’s Gujranwala office.

stories.title: Buddhist leaders explore Pakistan’s ancient Gandhara heritage
summary: Held under the theme "Towards a Shared Future", the dialogue aims to strengthen international cooperation for the preservation, promotion and global recognition of Gandhara's shared Buddhist heritage.

The engagements formed part of a broader effort to position Gandhara as a shared civilisational legacy and strengthen Pakistan's cultural outreach through heritage preservation, academic research, religious tourism and international collaboration.
The three-day dialogue brings together Buddhist religious leaders, scholars, heritage experts and Pakistani stakeholders.

stories.title: FCC directs LDA to stop ‘frivolous litigation’ against family of martyred national hero Rashid Minhas
summary: During subsequent execution proceedings, the LDA objected, arguing that the 14-marla plot in Gulberg-III, Lahore, was evacuee property acquired by the authority for the development of the Gulberg-III scheme.
The LHC had consequently directed the LDA to stop claiming ownership of the disputed land, which had already become part of the Gulberg-III scheme, the FCC observed.

The high court’s judgment was subsequently challenged by the LDA before the Supreme Court, which dismissed the petition, holding that the authority had no ownership rights over the land, as it had already been transferred by the Settlement Department to the occupants.

stories.title: Pakistan, Turkmenistan to convene steering committee for TAPI gas pipeline, stress engagement among partner countries
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday discussed the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline with a delegation led by Turkmenistan’s Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov.
The discussion took place at the 6th Session of the Pakistan–Turkmenistan Joint Intergovernmental Commission (JIC), which was held in Islamabad on Tuesday.
In June 2023, Pakistan and Turkmenistan signed a joint implementation plan to execute the TAPI gas pipeline project.

stories.title: PTI's Taimur Jhagra, Kamran Bangash arrested after PHC grants bail in Radio Pakistan attack case
summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders Taimur Saleem Jhagra and Kamran Bangash were arrested on Tuesday under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, after the Peshawar High Court granted them interim pre-arrest bail in the May 9, 2023, Radio Pakistan attack case.

Read: Peshawar ATC reissues arrest warrants for Sohail Afridi in Radio Pakistan attack case During the hearing before the ATC, lawyers representing the PTI leaders argued that the case had been revived nearly three years after the incident.

Two PTI leaders arrested under MPO Despite the high court's bail order in the Radio Pakistan case, police later arrested Jhagra and Bangash under separate warrants issued under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers, police clash in fresh wage protest
summary: Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed.
A wage board meeting scheduled for Monday was postponed after a member representing the garment workers said he was unwell, a source in BGMEA told AFP.
The country’s garment industry makes clothes for some of the world’s best-known brands but the sector has been marred by longstanding disputes over wages, working conditions and labour rights.

stories.title: ECP approves two-phase local polls in Punjab, first vote on Feb 7
summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Tuesday approved holding local government elections in Punjab in two phases, with the first phase scheduled for February 7, 2027.
In a letter issued to the Punjab chief secretary, the commission agreed to the provincial government’s proposal to divide the elections into two phases, each covering 18 district groups.
Read: PPP Punjab demands devolution of power to local govts The provincial government had initially agreed to hold the elections between December 15, 2026 and January 15, 2027.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank approves $500m loan to support Pakistan’s federal pension reforms
summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Tuesday approved a $500 million results-based loan to help Pakistan reform its federal civil pension system, the Manila-based lending agency said in a statement.
An earlier report by the ADB highlighted Pakistan’s weak pension and insurance systems.

Most government positions entail unfunded pensions, where pensions for current employees are financed through tax revenues, according to the report titled ‘Strengthening Pakistan’s Pension and Insurance Systems’.
